q: Which area of a bank processes, settles and reconciles transactions?
why: The back office handles processing, settlement and reconciliations.

q: Risk management and compliance usually sit in the…
why: The middle office manages risk and control.

q: Which division manages the bank's own liquidity and funding?
why: Treasury manages liquidity, funding and interest-rate risk.

q: What is the accounting equation?
why: The balance sheet always balances: Assets = Liabilities + Equity.

q: Which account types increase with a debit?
why: Assets and expenses increase with debits; liabilities, equity and revenue with credits.

q: A customer deposits $1,000 cash. How does the bank record it?
why: Cash (asset) increases with a debit; deposits owed to the customer (liability) increase with a credit.

q: Why does a bank 'credit' your account when you receive money?
options: Your deposit is a liability for the bank, and liabilities increase with credits
Credits always mean money in for everyone
why: Statements are written from the bank's perspective.

q: In double-entry bookkeeping, what must always be true?
options: Credits are recorded a day later
why: Every transaction has equal debits and credits.

q: What is a suspense account?
options: A temporary account for items not yet allocated to the correct account
A savings account with high interest
why: Suspense items should be cleared quickly; old balances are a red flag.

q: A trial balance checks that…
options: Total debit balances equal total credit balances across GL accounts
why: The trial balance lists all GL balances and confirms debits equal credits.

q: What is the relationship between the general ledger and sub-ledgers?
options: Sub-ledgers hold detail that summarizes into GL control accounts
The GL holds more detail than sub-ledgers
why: The GL is the master record; sub-ledgers hold transaction-level detail.

q: Recognizing an expense when it is incurred rather than when cash is paid is called…
why: Accruals match income and expenses to the period they belong to.

q: A wrong source-system-to-GL mapping is dangerous because…
options: Many transactions can post to the wrong account
why: Mappings drive bulk postings, so one error affects many entries.

q: What is a reconciliation 'break'?
options: An item that doesn't match between the two records
why: Breaks are exceptions that must be investigated.

q: An item is booked internally today and appears on the bank statement tomorrow. What type of break is this?
why: Timing differences usually clear on their own, but must be monitored.

q: The bank deducted a $15 fee from an incoming payment. What break type results?
why: The amounts differ by the fee.

q: Why are aged breaks a concern?
options: They may hide errors, fraud or real financial loss
why: The longer an item stays open, the harder it is to resolve and the greater the risk.

q: Comparing the GL control account balance to the total of the loans sub-ledger is which reconciliation?
why: It checks the GL agrees with its supporting detail.

q: Two companies in the same group disagree about what one owes the other. Which reconciliation resolves this?
why: Intercompany reconciliations match balances between group entities.

q: An Australian bank's USD account held at a New York bank is, from the Australian bank's view, a…
why: Nostro means 'ours': our account held at another bank.

q: From the New York bank's point of view, the same account is a…
why: Vostro means 'yours': your account held with us. Same account, two views.

q: The date when funds actually become available is the…
why: The value date determines availability and interest.

q: What does T+1 settlement mean?
options: Settlement one business day after the trade date
why: T is the trade date; +1 means the next business day.

q: AUD/USD = 0.65 means…
why: The first currency (base) is quoted in units of the second.

q: What is SWIFT?
options: A secure messaging network that sends payment instructions between banks
why: SWIFT carries messages; money settles through accounts and settlement systems.

q: Which ISO 20022 message replaces the MT103 customer credit transfer?
why: pacs.008 is the interbank customer credit transfer.

q: Which message is a bank-to-customer statement in ISO 20022?
why: camt.053 is the statement message, the ISO equivalent of MT940.

q: Why does ISO 20022 help reconciliation?
options: Richer, structured data such as references improves automatic matching
It removes the need for reconciliations
why: Structured remittance and party data make matching and screening more accurate.

q: Which US system provides high-value real-time gross settlement?
why: Fedwire is the Federal Reserve's RTGS system; ACH is batch.

q: Which of these is a US instant payment service available 24/7?
why: FedNow and RTP are US instant payment rails.

q: What does KYC stand for?
why: KYC verifies identity and understands customer activity.

q: What are the three stages of money laundering?
why: Criminals place cash, layer it through transactions, then integrate it into the economy.

q: The person who creates a payment cannot also approve it. This is…
why: SoD stops one person controlling a whole transaction.

q: One person prepares a reconciliation and another reviews and signs it off. This is the…
why: Maker-checker is a core banking control.

q: SOX section 404 requires public companies to…
options: Assess their internal controls over financial reporting
why: SOX 404 focuses on management's assessment of internal controls.

q: Internal audit belongs to which line of defense?
why: Internal audit provides independent assurance as the third line.

q: A reconciliation that finds errors after they happen is a…
why: Detective controls find issues; preventive controls stop them.

q: Which statement shows assets, liabilities and equity at a point in time?
why: The balance sheet is a snapshot.

q: Which statement separates operating, investing and financing activities?
why: The cash flow statement groups cash movements by activity.

q: A lower cost-to-income ratio means a bank is…
why: It spends less to earn each dollar of income.

q: Current assets $500k, current liabilities $250k. What is the current ratio?
Net interest margin measures…
options: Interest earned minus interest paid, relative to earning assets
why: NIM is a bank's core lending profitability.
